notes: EBIT is mapped to CF’s “Operating earnings” from the Consolidated Statements of Operations (FY2023–FY2025). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))
D&A is mapped to cash flow “Depreciation and amortization.” ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))

Capex is mapped to cash flow “Additions to property, plant and equipment” (absolute values; modeled as positive outflows in the DCF). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))

Net working capital (NWC) construction: NWC = (Total current assets − Cash and cash equivalents) − Total current liabilities, with an assumption of zero disclosed short-term borrowings (none presented as a separate current-borrowing line item in the referenced balance sheets). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))

FY2025 cash includes $130M held by the Blue Point joint venture (a consolidated VIE), which may slightly distort cash-to-enterprise value comparisons vs. a pure standalone cash figure. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))
Tax rate is set to CF’s 2025 effective tax rate (19.7%). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))

NOL balance uses state net operating loss and capital loss carryforwards of $53M (best available disclosed NOL-like figure). NOL utilization percent is not explicitly disclosed, so it is set to null. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))

Comps EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA are approximated using StockAnalysis EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA figures (not explicitly labeled NTM on the pages), so interpret as proxies. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ntr/statistics/))

catalysts: Yazoo City restart progress (timing/throughput) could swing both sales volumes and operating earnings vs. base-case normalization. ([ir.cfindustries.com](https://ir.cfindustries.com/Investors/news/news-details/2026/CF-Industries-Holdings-Inc--Reports-Full-Year-2025-Net-Earnings-of-1-46-Billion-Adjusted-EBITDA-of-2-89-Billion/default.aspx))
Improvement in global nitrogen pricing/spreads and natural gas input economics can rapidly impact EBIT for a commodity producer.

Execution on low-carbon ammonia investments (including Blue Point economics) could shift longer-duration growth expectations. ([ir.cfindustries.com](https://ir.cfindustries.com/Investors/news/news-details/2026/CF-Industries-Holdings-Inc--Reports-Full-Year-2025-Net-Earnings-of-1-46-Billion-Adjusted-EBITDA-of-2-89-Billion/default.aspx))
company_overview: CF Industries is a global manufacturer of hydrogen and nitrogen products with manufacturing complexes in the U.S., Canada, and the U.K. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))

The company operates an integrated ammonia-to-nitrogen value chain and also develops low-carbon ammonia initiatives. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))
In 2025, CF reported net sales of $7.084B and operating earnings (EBIT) of $2.300B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 results: net sales $7.08B; EBITDA $2.78B; adjusted EBITDA $2.89B, with $1.98B cash and $3.22B long-term debt at 12/31/2025. ([ir.cfindustries.com](https://ir.cfindustries.com/Investors/news/news-details/2026/CF-Industries-Holdings-Inc--Reports-Full-Year-2025-Net-Earnings-of-1-46-Billion-Adjusted-EBITDA-of-2-89-Billion/default.aspx))

2026 operating setup includes a Yazoo City, MS outage: management expects gross ammonia production of ~9.5 million tons in 2026, with production not expected to resume until at least Q4 2026. ([ir.cfindustries.com](https://ir.cfindustries.com/Investors/news/news-details/2026/CF-Industries-Holdings-Inc--Reports-Full-Year-2025-Net-Earnings-of-1-46-Billion-Adjusted-EBITDA-of-2-89-Billion/default.aspx))

Capital intensity is elevated: management projected ~ $1.3B total capital expenditures in 2026 (including Blue Point JV activity). ([ir.cfindustries.com](https://ir.cfindustries.com/Investors/news/news-details/2026/CF-Industries-Holdings-Inc--Reports-Full-Year-2025-Net-Earnings-of-1-46-Billion-Adjusted-EBITDA-of-2-89-Billion/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: EBIT margin durability: base case assumes margins normalize from the 2025 peak toward a mid-cycle level (~0.33 EBIT margin by 2030).

Low-cost North American manufacturing and distribution supports through-cycle profitability (reflected in stable DA% and capex as % of sales assumptions). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))

Investment-to-growth cadence: elevated capex supports expansion/low-carbon positioning, with the model gradually reducing capex intensity as projects mature. ([ir.cfindustries.com](https://ir.cfindustries.com/Investors/news/news-details/2026/CF-Industries-Holdings-Inc--Reports-Full-Year-2025-Net-Earnings-of-1-46-Billion-Adjusted-EBITDA-of-2-89-Billion/default.aspx))

Capital return remains a key pillar: FY2025 included $1.34B of share repurchases, supporting per-share value preservation. ([ir.cfindustries.com](https://ir.cfindustries.com/Investors/news/news-details/2026/CF-Industries-Holdings-Inc--Reports-Full-Year-2025-Net-Earnings-of-1-46-Billion-Adjusted-EBITDA-of-2-89-Billion/default.aspx))
key_risks: Commodity risk: unfavorable nitrogen pricing and/or natural gas cost volatility could compress EBIT margins below base-case.
Operational risk: additional outages, delays, or impairments could reduce volumes and increase maintenance/capex needs.
Tax and regulatory risk: changes to credits (e.g., clean energy tax regimes) or uncertain utilization of tax attributes could affect effective tax and cash taxes.

valuation_summary: DCF anchors on historical operating earnings (EBIT) conversion, with D&A and capex drawn from the company’s cash flow statements. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324404/000132440426000007/cf-20251231.htm))
Terminal value uses a Gordon-growth framework (2.0% terminal growth) with a base-case WACC of 9.5%, intended to reflect a cyclical industrial/commodity risk profile.
